newsitem.title: USA: McLeod wins PCS bids for 24 markets.
newsitem.headline: McLeod wins PCS bids for 24 markets.

text.p: McLeod Inc said Monday it successfully bid for 26 Personal Communications Services (PCS) licenses in 24 markets in a recent federal auction.

McLeod, a provider of integrated telecommunications services, said the licenses cover areas in Iowa, Illinois, Minnesota, Nebraska and South Dakota. The company said it will pay about $32.8 million for the licenses.
McLeod said providing wireless phone service is part of the company's strategy to provide one-stop telecommunications services to its customers.
The company said it will likely begin offering PCS in the Cedar Rapids and Iowa City, Iowa, markets.

"Now that the auction is complete, we are ready to move toward the design and development stages of our wireless plan in order to prepare for deployment of PCS technology," Stephen Gray, president and chief executive of McLeod, said in a statement.
